newsitem.title: THAILAND: Krungthai Thanakit says has bank licence approval.
newsitem.headline: Krungthai Thanakit says has bank licence approval.

text.p: State-backed Thai broker Krungthai Thanakit Plc is to be awarded a commercial banking licence for its 30-day government-appointed role in helping to stabilise the ailing Thai finance industry, the firm said on Sunday.

The broker is one of five large finance firms set to play a leading role in consolidating and supporting 16 financially distressed companies which were suspended from operations by the central bank on Friday.

"We have requested a commercial bank licence and already have a letter from the Ministry of Finance saying that one will be granted to us in connection with the consolidation process," the firm's President Phirasilp Subhapholsiri told a news conference on Sunday after meeting central bank officials.
The central bank has given the 16 ailing firms 14 days to merge, find foreign buyers, or face being taken over by the Bank of Thailand and absorbed by the selected stronger companies.

The Thai finance and securities sector is struggling to cope with declining revenues, high funding costs and a deterioration in asset quality as Thailand goes through its worst economic downturn for more than a decade.
"It is possible that the liabilities we will absorb from our fincos will exceed the sound assets," Phirasilp said.
"We will of course only proceed along this path if the issue is addressed to our satisfaction," he added.
It was as yet undecided which firms Krungthai Thanakit might absorb but it would prefer the largest of the 16, senior executives said.
Three large firms, Finance One Plc, General Finance and Securities Plc, and CMIC Finance and Securities Plc were among those suspended on Friday.
"There is some advantage to us being first in the queue in that we may to some extent be able to cherry pick the assets," one executive said.

In return for the bank licence for 30 days, Krungthai Thanakit will allow depositors of promissory notes issued by the 16 ailing firms to borrow against the notes at a 40 to 60 percent discount to their face value.
The Bank of Thailand will assist Krungthai Thanakit with additional funding requirements as necessary, Phirasilp said.
Krungthai Thanakit will charge note-holding borrowers 150 basis points over domestic commercial bank Minimum Overdraft Rates currently around 13.50 percent.
Notes can also be exchanged for those issued by one of the five larger finance companies designated by the central bank.
The four other firms are Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc, National Finance and Securities Plc, Nava Finance and Securities Plc, and Phatra Thanakit Plc.

The fate of a commercial bank licence awarded to a consortium headed by General Finance and Securities Plc earlier this year is uncertain, though executives said a consolidating group headed by National Finance and Securities Plc might now receive it.
